profile_text.body:
Speechmatics describes itself as a builder of speech-to-text APIs for real conversations, not clean demos. Its site says the technology understands accents, multiple speakers, and multilingual speech, and offers sub-second, speaker-aware speech-to-text and text-to-speech across 55+ languages. The company positions the API for live captions, voice agents, meeting notes, and contact center analytics, and says a single model can transcribe 55+ languages even when speakers switch languages naturally. It has introduced a model called Linden, described as purpose-built for voice agents, and a multilingual speech-to-text model with code-switching across 55+ languages, available in production preview starting with batch transcription. The site also describes a model called Melia 1, stating that on Arabic and English it runs at less than half the mixed error rate of the next best model, and on Mandarin and Tamil it switches more accurately than anything else tested.

The company's speech-to-text API converts spoken audio into written text inside an app, product, or workflow. Speechmatics says it can process recorded files or live audio and return transcripts for captions, search, analytics, records, and voice AI. The site compares 12 text-to-speech APIs, including ElevenLabs, Google Cloud, Amazon Polly, and Speechmatics, to help users choose a voice for their use case and budget.

Speechmatics was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Cambridge, UK. Its product is described as speech-to-text with real-time translation, accent-agnostic, UK-hosted, and GDPR.
